results.label: this tree ships the M111 calendar-read state vocabulary (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the parent tree IS the committed M110 release: it owns the two clocks and refuses the single knob, but it has no state vocabulary at all
the parent's own restart isolates its lazy M102 default strategy snapshot (and the sequence it moves) rather than merging it into the delta
the parent produced owned history to inherit: three closed trades and one account row at the M110 defaults
the parent's account pair defaults to 15/45 and the row carries both columns
ON THE PARENT the same failing read is the recorded FAIL-OPEN: a null blackout, an empty event list, no state, no reason and no note — the payload that reads exactly like a quiet week
the parent still echoes its pair on that path, which is why the two payloads are comparable line for line
ON THE DELIVERED TREE the identical read is `unknown`, with the reason and the sentence attached
and everything else about the payload is unchanged: same pair, same currencies, same empty lists, no invented release
the two payloads differ ONLY by the state and the failure it names, which is the whole change
M111 adds NO schema object of any kind and changes none: every table, index and trigger is byte-identical to the parent's
every inherited fact is byte-identical after the upgrade: a state that is derived on every read has nothing to store
the pair the trader stored is still the pair the app applies, and the read did not move it
a second open of the database is a no-op: same objects, same facts, same pair
the change is additive in the strongest sense available here: the PARENT's own code still reads the file the delivered tree wrote, and still reports its own quiet shape there
and there is nothing to migrate for it: no column anywhere stores a calendar state

scope: M111 migration: no schema change, and the same read answers differently: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
